title: EDGE-A1189 D breakout options vs forechecker
source_text: Defense work with two doing breakout options vs one forechecker. Options shown: Wheel, Counter, Over, Reverse, Go.
game_problem: Two defensemen read one forechecker and exit pressure with the best available breakout option.
representative_information: Forechecker route and pressure side, partner position, open side and exit lane.
player_decisions: Puck retriever reads pressure and selects wheel, counter, over, reverse or go; partner supports the chosen solution.
space_organization: Defensive-zone breakout area with two defensemen and one forechecker.
coach_notes: Do not call the solution. Vary the forechecker approach so the pressure creates the read.
adaptation_text: Coach spots the puck to a retrieval area. One forechecker pressures with a variable route. The two defensemen read the pressure and use any available source option to make a controlled exit. Success is a controlled carry or pass through the exit area; reset immediately from a different puck/pressure start.
source_boundary: Source supports the two-defenseman vs one-forechecker breakout framework and named options. Variable forechecker route, controlled-exit success condition and reset structure are Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A1700 2v2 Score on Any Net
source_text: Diagram labels the station: 2v2 score on any net.
game_problem: Maintain possession and exploit changing space when either available net can be attacked.
representative_information: Defenders, teammate support, open net, open lane and pressure direction.
player_decisions: Attackers choose which net to attack and when to switch; defenders protect immediate threats and recover when the point of attack changes.
space_organization: Small-area 2v2 station using the nets shown in the source diagram.
coach_notes: Keep the any-net rule. Avoid directing players to a specific net; the value is the constant read of pressure and open space.
adaptation_text: Run short 2v2 shifts. Either team may attack any available net in the station. On a goal, turnover out of bounds or coach whistle, immediately restart with a new puck to sustain decisions and repetitions.
source_boundary: The any-net 2v2 concept is source-derived. Shift length and immediate-restart language are Carolina EDGE organization notes.

title: EDGE-A196 4v2 Keepaway
source_text: RONDO / monkey in the middle. Variation 3: 4v2 keepaway.
game_problem: Four attackers maintain possession against two defenders in a confined area.
representative_information: Defender pressure, teammate availability, passing lane and support angle.
player_decisions: Possession players choose pass, hold or reposition; defenders choose pressure and lane denial.
space_organization: Confined/circle rondo shown in the source.
coach_notes: Reward movement after the pass and receiving positions that create two passing options.
adaptation_text: Use the source 4v2 keepaway. Change defenders on a clean win/interception or after a short work interval. Keep the area tight enough that support angles matter.
source_boundary: 4v2 keepaway is source-derived. Rotation and area-adjustment notes are Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A197 5v2 Pass-and-Move Keepaway
source_text: RONDO / monkey in the middle. Variation 2: 5v2 - pass and move.
game_problem: Keep possession while creating new passing lanes immediately after the puck moves.
representative_information: Two defenders, teammate spacing, open lane and movement after pass.
player_decisions: Players decide where to support after moving the puck; defenders decide when to pressure or protect lanes.
space_organization: Five possession players around a confined circle/area with two defenders inside.
coach_notes: The constraint is pass-and-move, not a prescribed route. Support should change with the puck and defender pressure.
adaptation_text: Run 5v2. After passing, the passer must relocate to create a new support angle. Defenders become possession players on a clean win/interception according to the coach's rotation.
source_boundary: 5v2 pass-and-move is source-derived. Rotation wording is Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A198 5v3 Rondo / Power-Play Spacing
source_text: RONDO / monkey in the middle. Variation 1: larger spaced area 5v3 - PP, players move w/o puck.
game_problem: Maintain 5v3 possession while creating power-play support through off-puck movement.
representative_information: Three defenders, pressure side, teammate spacing and available seams.
player_decisions: Possession players move to open passing lanes and choose when to move the puck; defenders pressure or protect interior lanes.
space_organization: Larger spaced possession area shown in the source.
coach_notes: Emphasize off-puck movement and spacing rather than standing in fixed power-play spots.
adaptation_text: Play 5v3 possession in the larger source area. Possession team scores by maintaining connected support and moving the puck through pressure; reset or rotate after a clean defensive win.
source_boundary: 5v3 PP-style rondo and off-puck movement are source-derived. Scoring/reset language is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A218 3v3 Two-Gate Puck Support
source_text: 3v3 with 2 gates out wide. Players must pass or carry the puck through either gate when entering the other side of the ice. Focus on taking puck wide, triangle, support.
game_problem: Use width and support to move possession through one of two wide gates.
representative_information: Defenders, two gate options, teammate support and available width.
player_decisions: Puck carrier chooses which gate and whether to pass or carry; teammates create triangle support and defenders protect space.
space_organization: Small-area 3v3 with two wide gates connecting the playing sides.
coach_notes: Do not designate a gate. The pressure should make the better gate emerge.
adaptation_text: Use the source rules unchanged. Restart quickly after goals, out-of-bounds pucks or clear possession changes to maximize repetitions.
source_boundary: Core rules and focus are source-derived. Quick-restart guidance is Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A219 Red Baron 4v3 Possession Support
source_text: Red Baron: Players play 3v3 with the Red Baron playing offense with whichever team has possession of the puck. At all times the Red Baron is on offense so the team with possession always has a 4v3 advantage. Concepts: puck support, power play, penalty kill, transition.
game_problem: Use an always-offense neutral player to create and exploit 4v3 possession advantages.
representative_information: Possession change, defender pressure, Red Baron location and teammate spacing.
player_decisions: Possession team uses the neutral support; defenders protect dangerous space; all players transition immediately when possession changes.
space_organization: 3v3 small-area game plus one neutral Red Baron who always joins the team in possession.
coach_notes: The key transfer is transition: the Red Baron changes teams instantly with possession.
adaptation_text: Use the source rules unchanged. Keep shifts short and restart quickly so possession changes happen often.
source_boundary: Rules and concepts are source-derived. Shift/restart guidance is Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A220 Ringette Circle Keepaway with Outside Support
source_text: Players on inside play keepaway with ringet. Players on outside move around circle and pass through the middle.
game_problem: Maintain possession inside a confined circle while using moving outside support.
representative_information: Inside pressure, moving outside support players and passing windows through the circle.
player_decisions: Inside players choose when to protect, move or use outside support; outside players move to create new passing windows.
space_organization: Inside players in the faceoff circle; outside support players move around the circle.
coach_notes: Keep outside support moving; avoid fixed passing spots.
adaptation_text: Run the source ringette keepaway. Award continued possession when inside players connect through moving outside support; rotate inside/outside roles on a coach interval or turnover.
source_boundary: Inside/outside ringette keepaway is source-derived. Rotation/scoring language is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A221 Board Puck Retrieval Under Pressure
source_text: Coach dumps puck so it lands right against the boards. One player retrieves it - look over shoulder, angle out and scoop puck from boards (deep knee bend), keep skates parallel to boards, look up and pass to coach. Add a chaser without contact so the puck retriever looks over their shoulder and reads which way they should angle on the boards.
game_problem: Retrieve a board puck while scanning pressure and escape to the safer side.
representative_information: Puck location on boards, chaser approach and available escape side.
player_decisions: Retriever shoulder-checks and chooses the escape angle; chaser pressures without contact.
space_organization: Board-side retrieval station with coach as pass target.
coach_notes: The second progression is the representative version: the chaser's approach must change the retriever's solution.
adaptation_text: Begin with the source technical retrieval only as needed, then move quickly to the no-contact chaser progression. Score the rep when the retriever scans before contact, escapes away from pressure and completes the outlet.
source_boundary: Source supplies both the technical retrieval and live no-contact chaser progression. Success criteria wording is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A222 Look-Bump-Check Angling
source_text: LOOK-BUMP-CHECK: players next to each other, coach dumps puck into corner. Players look to see where the other player is, bumps them right before they get the puck. Angle down the boards with puck and race to dot. Player without puck tries to angle other player off the puck up the boards.
game_problem: Win a loose puck, establish body position and then angle/protect along the boards.
representative_information: Loose puck location, opponent position, boards and race target.
player_decisions: Players scan before contact, compete for body position, then puck carrier protects while opponent angles.
space_organization: Corner/board battle station finishing with an angling race toward the dot.
coach_notes: Apply age-appropriate contact rules. The scan before body contact is essential.
adaptation_text: Use the source sequence with short competitive reps. If body contact is not appropriate for the group, replace the bump with legal body-positioning/containment while preserving the read and angling problem.
source_boundary: Source rules are preserved. Age-appropriate non-contact substitution is Carolina EDGE safety adaptation.

title: EDGE-A291 1v1 Tire Puck-Protection Game
source_text: Game 3 is all about 1 on 1. We are looking to develop puck handling and protection skills here. Tight turns and evasions are key along with developing a strong base using the edges of the skates to drive around the opposing player. Each 1 on 1 pairing has a tyre. In order to score the player must drive their stick and the puck onto their opposing players tyre.
game_problem: Protect and maneuver the puck in 1v1 pressure to reach the opponent's tire target.
representative_information: Opponent body/stick position, tire target and available escape space.
player_decisions: Puck carrier uses turns/evasions to create target access; defender protects the tire and pressures the puck.
space_organization: Small-area 1v1; each player/pair has a tire scoring target.
coach_notes: Reward possession and evasive movement, not simply racing at the tire.
adaptation_text: Use the source rules unchanged with short shifts and immediate puck restarts.
source_boundary: Game rules and teaching purpose are source-derived. Shift/restart guidance is Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A292 1v1 to 2v1 Support Game
source_text: Game 4 is all about creating 2 on 1 opportunities which in turn develops their awareness of support and then how to use that support. Passing skills are essential along with a good quick take off to get around the opposing player. Game description - 1 on 1 inside the area, in order to score a player must pass to their team mate standing on the outside and receive the puck back.
game_problem: Turn a pressured 1v1 into a give-and-go 2v1 by recognizing and using outside support.
representative_information: Defender position, outside teammate, passing lane and return lane.
player_decisions: Puck carrier decides when/how to use outside support and where to move for the return; defender manages both puck and return route.
space_organization: 1v1 inside a small area with a teammate outside as support.
coach_notes: Outside player should support the puck, not stand in one fixed passing window.
adaptation_text: Use the source scoring rule. Rotate the outside support frequently so every player experiences both support and pressure roles.
source_boundary: Core rule and purpose are source-derived. Rotation guidance is Carolina EDGE organization guidance.

title: EDGE-A293 3v3 Area-Drive Support Game
source_text: Game 5 is really geared to develop a drive for players to get into an area, for example supporting the puck down low in the corner or even the front of the net. 3 v 3 in the small area. Each team looks to score by passing the puck into the opponents area to a team mate. This game can easily be adapted to have both areas open for both teams to score. No non puck possession team players are allowed in the area.
game_problem: Create off-puck support by timing movement into a protected scoring area.
representative_information: Puck location, protected scoring area, defender positioning and teammate timing.
player_decisions: Possession team decides when/where to enter the scoring area; defenders deny passing lanes without entering the restricted area.
space_organization: 3v3 small-area game with a designated scoring/support area.
coach_notes: The restricted-area rule should create timing and support, not camping. Encourage exits/re-entries if the passing lane closes.
adaptation_text: Use the source rules. Optionally open both scoring areas to both teams as the source suggests once players understand the timing problem.
source_boundary: Rules and optional both-areas variation are source-derived. Coaching note is Carolina EDGE guidance.

title: EDGE-A294 3v3 Coach-Pass Pivot Game
source_text: Game 1 is designed to develop movement in the offensive zone. Awareness of the puck is key. 3 on 3 below the tires; in order to score the players pass the puck to the coach and then that team has to pivot to the outside and find the big ice (space) to receive the pass back. Once received they may shoot. Here we work on pivots, passing + receiving, shooting, tight turns, evasion, communication and supporting the puck carrier.
game_problem: Create space and support off a coach give-and-go before attacking the net.
representative_information: Coach outlet, defender pressure, outside space and return passing lane.
player_decisions: Possession players decide who supports outside and where to re-enter; defenders recover as the point of attack changes.
space_organization: 3v3 below the source tires/line with coach as an outlet and net to attack.
coach_notes: The coach pass is a trigger to expand into space, not a scripted route.
adaptation_text: Use the source rules. Coach varies return pass timing/location so players must scan and support rather than run a preset pattern.
source_boundary: Core game description is source-derived. Variable return-pass guidance is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A295 3v3 Seam / Timing Game
source_text: Game 2 has been developed to develop timing and passing into areas. This is what I call the seem game; this helps the goalies work on their lateral movement and helps the players find the big ice. 3 v 3, the ice is halved by 2 tyres, in order to score the pass must go from one side to the other. This teaches players to be aware of where they are in the zone. They cant score if all 3 guys are on the same side.
game_problem: Create width and timing by moving the puck across a divided 3v3 area before scoring.
representative_information: Defenders, two sides of the area, seam between tires, teammate spacing and goalie movement.
player_decisions: Players decide when/how to move the puck across the seam and how to occupy both sides to create a scoring chance.
space_organization: 3v3 area divided into two sides by two tires with a net/goalie.
coach_notes: Do not tell players who must cross. Let spacing and defender pressure determine the solution.
adaptation_text: Use the source cross-side scoring requirement unchanged. Restart quickly and encourage players to occupy both sides before the puck arrives.
source_boundary: Core rules and purpose are source-derived. Restart/spacing emphasis is Carolina EDGE guidance.

title: EDGE-A346 Confined-Area Angling and Puck Protection
source_text: In a confined area, one player starts with the puck along the boards, the other player must angle and perform a body contact technique. The player with the puck also uses puck protection and escape moves to make the task more difficult.
game_problem: Protect the puck along the boards while an opponent angles and closes space in a confined area.
representative_information: Opponent angle, boards, available escape space and puck position.
player_decisions: Puck carrier chooses protection/escape move; defender adjusts angle and gap to contain and separate.
coach_notes: Use age-appropriate legal contact. The defender should angle based on the carrier's escape rather than follow a prescribed path.
adaptation_text: Use the source 1v1. Score short reps by possession retained/escaped versus legal containment or puck win. Rotate roles after each rep.
source_boundary: Core 1v1 and teaching purpose are source-derived. Scoring/rotation language is Carolina EDGE adaptation.
